UK Voters Await Results: Timeline for England, Scotland and Wales Election Outcomes

2026-05-08 | Politics

Voters in England, Scotland and Wales went to the polls today for a series of local and devolved elections, with counting set to begin as soon as the polls closed at 10 p.m. BST. Electoral Commission officials said that the first batch of results—primarily from smaller wards and constituencies with low postal‑vote volumes—will start appearing on live feeds around midnight.

In England, the biggest delay is expected from the large urban areas where postal ballots remain to be processed. "We anticipate a clear picture by 2 a.m. for most English councils, but the final counts in cities like Birmingham and Manchester may not be confirmed until early morning," said Sarah Hughes, a senior analyst at the Electoral Reform Society.

Scotland’s vote count for the Scottish Parliament constituencies will follow a similar pattern, with the first results expected around 12:30 a.m. and a more comprehensive outlook by 3 a.m. "The Highlands and Islands tend to report later due to geographic dispersal of polling stations," noted Dr. Iain MacLeod, politics professor at the University of Edinburgh.

Welsh officials have indicated that the Senedd election results will be trickling in from 1 a.m., with the majority of constituencies reporting by 4 a.m. However, the counting of regional list votes could extend the process into the late morning. "Postal votes in Wales have risen sharply this year, which adds a layer of complexity," warned Elinor Davies, head of the Welsh Local Government Association.
